normal.name: Tamagotchi Vibe 🎮
normal.text: I found a CRT TV in my grandma’s attic last week. Plugged in my old SNES—the screen flickered, then Mario slid into frame. That warm buzz felt like coming home. Does nostalgia ever beat the actual game for you? Play: https://t.me/the_tamagochi_game_bot?start=bsky_en1

normal.name: Rumbleminze
normal.text: How does NES hide the bottom of the dog on this screen? Most games I've seen do this by turning off sprites on that line with a sprite 0 hit triggered write. However Duck Hunt does it with 0 writes to any hardware registers outside of vblank! Answer in thread!

normal.name: Foltrovv
normal.text: It finally feels like October and I want to hunker down with a video game. Something nostalgic, cozy, and spooky. I want vibes that send me back to a Saturday morning with donuts and the smell of a CRT warming up.

normal.name: SkeleGhost
normal.text: The Toy Story game for the SNES, a game I played a lot as a kid, just released on Steam in a $30 retro game pack. So, feeling nostalgic... I dug out my original SNES and fired it up! Lo and behold, it still works! Ah, the memories of fun and cruel difficulty to be relived!🥹

normal.name: Cameron Kennedy
normal.text: Old games media was always a major inspiration for the look of the show for me. Over a year ago I started collecting pics of old game magazines and game ads. This was always going to be such a nostalgic show, it felt right to show love to games' history, games media history, and the guys' history.
